blocking.why: pause() is guardian-only and cancels every live proposal in one call; the loop is in the guardian's own tx, so the guardian controls whether/how it runs and can pause before the flood.
execute() requires the proposal to still be in _liveProposals and ready; pause() deletes timestamps and removes all ids, so flooded proposals cannot execute after a successful pause.
cancel() is safe-only and per-id; the team regaining the Safe via recovery spell can cancel individually, and the report's own scenario concedes recovery succeeds.

missing.resolves_when: A test shows pause() reverting/OOG on a proposal set the attacker can create, or that the attacker can schedule after pause and execute before the guardian can act.

evidence.claim: Timelock.pause() iterates over the unbounded _liveProposals set, so a hot signer (or compromised hot signer key) can spam schedule() to make pause() exceed the block gas limit, defeating the guardian's emergency pause.
evidence.known: If the cold signers are malicious or compromised, they can execute transactions to compromise the system if neither recovery spells or the guardian are used

blocking.why: schedule() is external onlySafe whenNotPaused; hot signers cannot add proposals.
scheduleBatch() is external onlySafe whenNotPaused; same restriction.
executeWhitelisted is the hot signer path and does not touch _liveProposals.
